QuestionText: Which part of the Central Processing Unit (CPU) is responsible for performing mathematical calculations like addition, subtraction, and logical comparisons such as matching or sorting data?
Explanation: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) handles all arithmetic calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical operations (AND, OR, NOT, comparisons) within the CPU.

QuestionText: The Control Unit (CU) acts as the supervisor or 'brain director' of the computer. What is its primary function?
Options: A) It permanently stores user files when the computer turns off.
B) It directs and coordinates the flow of data and instructions between all computer components.
C) It displays sharp graphics and videos on the screen.
D) It converts mechanical typing into physical ink on paper.
Explanation: The Control Unit does not process data itself; instead, it manages, coordinates, and directs the movement of signals across different hardware units like a traffic cop.

QuestionText: What is the large, primary circuit board inside a computer that connects the CPU, memory, hard drive, and all other internal and external peripherals together?
Explanation: The Motherboard (or system board) serves as the main communication spine through which all internal components and external devices interact with one another.

QuestionText: Why is Random Access Memory (RAM) classified as a 'volatile' form of computer memory?
Options: A) It can easily catch fire if the computer overheats.
B) It automatically expands its size when running large games.
C) It completely loses all stored data as soon as the power supply is turned off.
D) It cannot be modified or updated by the user.
Explanation: Volatile memory requires continuous electrical power to maintain its state. When the computer shuts down, everything stored temporarily in RAM vanishes instantly.

QuestionText: Which type of internal computer memory contains the permanent, built-in startup instructions (such as BIOS) that help boot up the system when you hit the power button?
Explanation: ROM holds crucial start-up instructions manufactured directly onto a chip. This data is non-volatile, meaning it remains intact even without electricity.

QuestionText: While working on an unsaved school report in MS Word, sudden power failure turns off your computer. Where was that unsaved report actively residing right before the crash?
Options: B) On the physical optical disc drive
C) In the volatile RAM memory
D) Permanently written to the Hard Disk
Explanation: Active applications and unsaved progress live in RAM. Since RAM is volatile, unexpected power cuts instantly wipe out any data that hasn't been saved to permanent storage.

QuestionText: What is the primary internal data storage device found inside almost every desktop tower, used to permanently store the operating system, apps, games, and files?
Explanation: The Hard Disk Drive (HDD) is the primary, high-capacity non-volatile magnetic storage unit used to keep systems, programs, and custom user data saved permanently.

QuestionText: Modern computers often swap older magnetic Hard Disk Drives (HDDs) for Solid-State Drives (SSDs). What is a major hardware advantage of an SSD?
Options: A) It uses heavy spinning magnetic discs to save power.
B) It has no moving parts, making it much faster, quieter, and more durable than an HDD.
C) It only operates when the computer is completely disconnected from power.
D) It can only hold text documents but not images or video files.
Explanation: SSDs read and write data using flash memory chips instead of mechanical spinning magnetic platters, delivering much faster boot and loading times with zero noise.

QuestionText: Which computer component converts high-voltage Alternating Current (AC) electricity from your home wall outlet into lower-voltage Direct Current (DC) electricity needed by internal PC components?
Options: B) SMPS / PSU (Switched-Mode Power Supply / Power Supply Unit)
Explanation: The SMPS/PSU acts as the electrical power plant of the system, converting raw wall power into clean, precise voltages safe for fragile computer circuits.

QuestionText: What type of hardware device translates real-world movements, physical traits, text sheets, or voice signals into electronic binary data for a computer to process?
Explanation: Input devices (like keyboards, mice, microphones, scanners) convert physical user inputs into electronic binary signals that the computer can decode.

QuestionText: Which specialized device is designed to scan printed paper documents or photos and convert them into digital image files on your computer?
Explanation: An optical scanner shines light on physical paper pages to record their imagery and convert them into digital files (like PDFs or JPEGs).

QuestionText: An Optical Character Recognition (OCR) scanner is most commonly used for which of the following real-world tasks?
Options: A) Playing highly complex video games with a stick controller
B) Reading printed or handwritten paper text and converting it into editable digital text files
C) Recording high-definition surround sound music
D) Cooling down an overheated processor core
Explanation: OCR systems use intelligent software scanning to turn flat pixel images of letters into selectable, interactive, and editable text files.

QuestionText: When checking out items at a supermarket, the cashier points a laser gun device at vertical black-and-white lines on a product package. What input device is being used?
Explanation: A barcode reader uses laser reflections to interpret the width of printed black-and-white stripes, instantly finding the item ID in the store inventory database.

QuestionText: Which specialized scanning device is used by bank machines to read unique, computerized routing numbers printed at the bottom of paper checks using iron-infused magnetic ink?
Options: B) MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) Reader
C) OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) Sheet Machine
Explanation: MICR technology reads characters printed in specialized magnetic ink, which is standard practice in banking to prevent fraud on check transactions.

QuestionText: When you take a multiple-choice Olympiad exam on a paper sheet where you fill in round bubbles with a pencil, what device automatically scans and grades your paper?
Explanation: OMR readers project light onto the paper sheet to detect the dark filled-in circle markers, allowing rapid grading of standardized tests.

QuestionText: Which input device allows designers, architects, and artists to draw freehand artwork directly onto a flat screen or pad using a pen-like stylus?
Explanation: Graphic tablets map the location of a specialized stylus pen onto digital canvasses, allowing highly detailed digital sketching and blueprint drafting.

QuestionText: Which component is an output device used specifically to generate physical paper records (hard copies) of computer data?
Explanation: Printers are classic output devices that transfer soft copy digital files onto physical pages to generate hard copies.

QuestionText: How do non-impact printers (like modern Laser and Inkjet printers) differ fundamentally from older impact printers (like Dot-Matrix printers)?
Options: A) Non-impact printers strike an inked ribbon physically against paper to stamp letters.
B) Non-impact printers use non-electrical gears made of wood.
C) Non-impact printers spray ink or use lasers to bake toner powder onto paper without hitting the page directly.
D) Non-impact printers are much slower and louder than impact printers.
Explanation: Non-impact printers create text and shapes without physical strikes, making them significantly faster, quieter, and sharper than older pin-striking dot-matrix impact printers.

QuestionText: An engineer needs to print huge, ultra-precise architectural blueprints, construction maps, or outdoor banners. Which high-grade output device should they use?
Explanation: Plotters are specialized line-drawing machines that use continuous vector lines to create gigantic engineering charts and architectural blueprints.

QuestionText: The physical clarity and detail of images displayed on a monitor screen are measured by the number of individual color dots it can show. What are these dots called?
Explanation: Pixels (short for Picture Elements) are the tiny individual illuminated dots that make up a digital image on screen displays.

QuestionText: What classification applies to a touch-sensitive interactive smartboard used inside a classroom?
Options: C) Both an Input and Output Device
Explanation: Touchscreens output visual computer responses on screen while simultaneously accepting physical touch input from fingers or markers, serving dual roles.

QuestionText: Which electronic slot or plug interface on the back of a computer tower is most commonly used today to connect modern keyboards, mice, flash drives, and printers?
Explanation: USB ports have become the industry standard connection method for almost all hot-swappable external hardware accessories.

QuestionText: What type of port would you use to plug a digital monitor or projector into a computer to send high-definition audio and video over a single cable?
Explanation: HDMI ports transmit uncompressed high-def digital video and multi-channel audio data across one unified connection cord.

QuestionText: Arrange these computer storage capacities in ascending order (from smallest to largest): 1 Gigabyte (GB), 1 Kilobyte (KB), 1 Terabyte (TB), 1 Megabyte (MB).
Explanation: Memory scale steps up by standard factors of 1024: Kilobyte (KB) is smallest, followed by Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), and Terabyte (TB) as the largest.

QuestionText: A single byte of computer data consists of how many individual binary digits (bits)?
Explanation: One basic byte contains exactly 8 individual bits (0s or 1s), which is the storage volume required to represent a single character like the letter 'A'.

QuestionText: Exactly how many Megabytes (MB) make up 1 full Gigabyte (GB) of standard computer storage?
Explanation: In computing binary systems, 1 Gigabyte is equal to $2^{10}$ Megabytes, which scales to exactly 1024 MB.

QuestionText: What type of expansion card can be plugged into a motherboard slot to let heavy 3D action video games render fast, beautiful images without lagging?
Options: B) Dedicated Graphics Card / GPU (Video Card)
Explanation: A dedicated graphics card contains its own high-speed processor (GPU) and VRAM memory specialized for generating 3D textures and smooth frames on screen.

QuestionText: Why do high-speed modern CPU chips always have a metal block with fins (heatsink) and a running fan attached directly on top of them?
Options: A) To blow dust into the computer case panels.
B) To distribute electric current from the wall adapter safely.
C) To draw away and dissipate the extreme heat generated during processing, keeping the CPU cool.
D) To help the CPU spin around faster.
Explanation: CPUs contain millions of micro-scale electrical pathways that produce significant thermal energy. Without a heatsink and fan drawing heat away, the chip would quickly overheat and shut down.

QuestionText: What are the fast, internal storage compartments built directly inside the CPU chip itself, used to hold tiny instructions and data values the ALU is calculating at that exact microsecond?
Explanation: Registers are the fastest, smallest memory units located directly inside the CPU structure to hold immediate items needed for ongoing calculations.

QuestionText: Which type of external storage device uses laser beam technology to read and write digital data on shiny circular discs?
Explanation: CDs, DVDs, and Blu-rays are optical media. They contain micro-tracks read by a physical laser lens assembly inside the disc drive player.

QuestionText: What type of component is a computer flash drive (Pen Drive) which plugs into a USB port?
Options: B) Non-volatile secondary storage using solid-state flash memory
Explanation: Pen drives are portable secondary storage devices that don't lose data when unplugged. They use non-volatile flash chips to store files indefinitely.

QuestionText: Identify the storage medium that can hold the greatest volume of data from the choices listed.
Options: C) 2 Terabyte External Hard Drive (2000 GB)
D) 32 Gigabyte USB Pen Drive (32 GB)
Explanation: 2 Terabytes equals roughly 2048 Gigabytes, which is significantly larger than a 32 GB pen drive, a 4.7 GB DVD, or a 700 MB CD.

QuestionText: Which internal system component acts as an electronic highway, consisting of copper traces on the motherboard used to move data bits between the CPU, memory, and devices?
Explanation: The system bus is the group of physical parallel wires or traces through which data, addresses, and control signals pass within the PC circuitry.

QuestionText: What does a computer's 'Cache Memory' do to speed up processing tasks?
Options: A) It prints out hard copies at high speeds.
B) It acts as an ultra-fast buffer between the CPU and RAM, storing frequently used instructions so the CPU doesn't have to wait.
C) It prevents online hackers from seeing the screen.
D) It cleans out dust build-up from internal fans.
Explanation: Cache memory is tiny, ultra-fast static RAM (SRAM) sitting close to the CPU core. It mirrors active data chunks from the slower primary RAM to boost execution speeds.

QuestionText: Which type of device would you plug into a network slot (Ethernet port) on a motherboard to let a computer communicate over wires with other local devices?
Explanation: The Network Interface Card (NIC) handles wired or wireless data packet transactions to connect a computer to a local network or modem router.

QuestionText: What type of data storage metric equals exactly half of one standard 8-bit byte (meaning a group of 4 bits)?
Explanation: In computer architecture, a group of four binary digits (bits) is officially known as a 'nibble'.

QuestionText: Which device reads patterns of pencil marks made on specialized application or contest registration forms?
Explanation: An OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) reader is custom-built to check for the presence or absence of dark marks in predefined areas on a sheet.

QuestionText: Which computer device serves as a biometrics-based input hardware component to safeguard modern laptops?
Explanation: Fingerprint scanners capture biometric skin patterns and convert them into digital signatures to securely verify user identity.

QuestionText: What type of device is a flatbed optical scanner?
Options: A) Output device used to show videos.
B) Storage medium for system backup archives.
C) Input device used to convert hard copies into soft copies.
D) Processing module within the CPU core.
Explanation: Scanners take physical materials (hard copies) and convert them into digital data files (soft copies) for storage or editing on a computer.

QuestionText: Identify the device from the options below that functions as a legacy 'impact printer'.
Explanation: Dot-matrix printers are impact printers because they use small pins to strike an inked ribbon against a page to form letters.

QuestionText: A user needs to choose a secondary storage system that can easily transfer small school files between different computers without needing an internet connection. Which option is best?
Explanation: USB flash drives are compact, rewritable, non-volatile, and highly portable, making them ideal for carrying files between different computers.

QuestionText: If a computer has high speed RAM but lacks a working Secondary Storage unit, what will it be unable to do?
Options: A) Perform arithmetic comparisons in the ALU.
B) Accept typing inputs from a USB keyboard.
C) Permanently save files, documents, and programs for later use after power down.
D) Display color pixels on a monitor panel.
Explanation: Primary storage (RAM) is volatile and cannot save data long-term. Without secondary storage (like an HDD or SSD), all files would disappear every time the computer is turned off.

QuestionText: What does the abbreviation 'BIOS', stored securely inside the motherboard's ROM chip, stand for?
Explanation: BIOS stands for Basic Input Output System. It initializes hardware components during the boot process to ensure everything is working before loading the main OS.

QuestionText: What do the three core steps of a standard computer's processing cycle stand for in order?
Explanation: Computers operate on the IPO cycle: they take raw data (Input), process it using the CPU (Processing), and produce results (Output).

QuestionText: Which type of monitor is thin, flat, lightweight, and uses liquid crystals to create the images displayed on modern laptop and desktop screens?
Explanation: LCD monitors replaced bulky CRT screens by using a liquid crystal solution sandwiched between polarizing sheets to efficiently display images.

QuestionText: What physical hardware component links external devices to the computer's system bus through the back of a computer casing?
Explanation: Ports are external interface slots on a computer case that allow you to plug in device cables to establish a connection with the internal system bus.

QuestionText: Which storage device is an example of flash-based non-volatile memory used primarily inside digital cameras and smartphones to store photos and videos?
Explanation: Secure Digital (SD) memory cards use solid-state flash technology to provide reliable, compact storage for portable electronic devices.

QuestionText: Why is primary memory (RAM) much closer to the CPU in terms of the computer's architecture compared to secondary memory (HDDs/SSDs)?
Options: A) Because RAM chips are much heavier than hard drives.
B) To allow the CPU to read and write data at high speeds, keeping up with processing demands.
C) Because RAM can only store files when the computer is completely turned off.
D) To protect the RAM chips from getting dusty.
Explanation: The CPU operates at incredibly high speeds. It reads active data directly from RAM because accessing secondary storage devices like hard drives is much slower and would cause a performance bottleneck.

QuestionText: Which of the following units is the largest in terms of data storage capacity?
Explanation: 1 Gigabyte is equal to 1024 Megabytes. This makes it larger than 500 Megabytes, 1 Megabyte, or 1024 Kilobytes (which is exactly 1 Megabyte).

QuestionText: A computer device that can display text or graphics onto a wall or large sheet so a whole room of people can view it together is called a:
Explanation: Projectors take the video signals generated by a computer and beam them onto large flat surfaces, making them ideal for classroom or boardroom presentations.
